messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] display Graphics
parts:
On findOverlaps, you should check the documentation for findOverlaps() function. I think it is clear there. But briefly, The returned matrix is showing which row of gr1 is overlapping with which row of gene.obj. By the way, you should overlap elements in the gene.obj separately, it contains a list of GRanges objects you are not interested in overlaps of all of them.
do something like:
findOverlaps(gr1, gene.obj$exons) #


On duplicated bases in methylDiff object, this is likely a problem that occurred in the upstream. I guess some values are duplicated in methylBase object and likely because they are duplicated in methylRaw objects. So you need to find out why they are duplicated in the beginning. Are you using read.bismark() function or did you create a methylation ratio/percentage text file on your own?

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] display Graphics
parts:
There are no duplicates in these datasets. Only thing that is odd and may be causing a problem is that you don't have "chr" string in front of your chromosome names. Currently, R thinks that the "id" column is numeric where it should be character or factor.

You can run read.bismark, save the methylation calls as text files, and then add the "chr" string via awk (should be added to both id column and chr columns). This will also cause problems in the downstream analysis where gene annotation files usually have the "chr" string in the chromosome names. 

If the problem persists, generate a subsample of the dataset that reproduces the problem and your code (this is important!!), and reply to this thread.

Best,
Altuna
